paper.title: Minimum number of nights for reliable estimation of habitual sleep using a consumer sleep tracker
paper.claim: Demonstrates that minimum nights for habitual sleep estimates depend on the measure, aggregation window, and target reliability.
paper.population: The paper studied consumer-tracker sleep in adults; this package uses generated participants only.
paper.referenceStandard: Published minimum-night methodology; deterministic participant-grouped generated fixture for this package.
paper.relationEvidence: Independent Apache-2.0 implementation of a participant-level ICC reliability example; it does not reproduce the paper's device, cohort, data, or exact model.

compatibility.window: Exactly seven distinct nightly measurements per participant.
compatibility.preprocessing: Keep each participant's nights together; calculate balanced ICC(1,1); bootstrap participants rather than nights; abstain below twenty participants.
mismatches: Generated duration values do not validate any Brainstem device or cohort.
The paper's consumer device, population, dataset, and exact statistical model are not reproduced.
A protected scientific review must freeze the production estimator and uncertainty method.

cohort.output: Aggregate reliability curve and minimum-night guidance; no participant or nightly rows.

personal.output: Owner-only descriptive trend with cohort placement withheld until the reviewed metric-specific night requirement is met.
